questions.q: What is the primary meaning of the **Rule of Law**?
options: The law only applies to the poor and vulnerable citizens
The principle that all people and institutions are subject to and accountable to a supreme law that is fairly applied and enforced
A military decree that suspends the constitution completely
The absolute power of the President to write and execute any law personally
questions.explain: The **Rule of Law** is the democratic principle that implies the absolute supremacy or predominance of regular law as opposed to the influence of arbitrary power. Everyone is subject to it.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In Civic Education, a **Law** is best defined as:
options: A temporary suggestion made by wealthy businessmen
A body of enacted or customary rules recognized by a community as binding, which regulates human conduct
A personal opinion written by a judge during an election
A verbal promise made by politicians during political campaigns
questions.explain: A **Law** is a formal, legally binding system of rules established and enforced by a governing authority to regulate behavior and maintain social order.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following perfectly describes **Arbitrary Rule**, which the Rule of Law actively opposes and seeks to prevent?
options: A government executing its duties strictly according to the written constitution
Judges using legal precedence to issue fair judgments
A leader exercising unchecked, dictatorial power based solely on personal whim rather than written law
Holding periodic free and fair elections
questions.explain: **Arbitrary rule** is a system of government where the leader's decisions are not restrained by law. The Rule of Law combats this by enforcing constitutional limits on power.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The fundamental concept of **'Equality of all citizens before the law'** guarantees that:
options: No individual, regardless of their wealth, class, or political position, is above the laws of the land
All citizens must possess exactly the same amount of money
Only government officials are exempt from paying traffic fines
Minors and adults must receive exactly the same punishments for any crime
questions.explain: **Equality before the law** (Legal Egalitarianism) is the pillar of the Rule of Law asserting that every individual, rich or poor, leader or follower, is subject to the exact same legal codes and judicial processes.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Under the Rule of Law, what is the legitimate, constitutional process for administering **punishment for breaking the law**?
options: The police executing the suspect immediately upon arrest
An angry mob carrying out jungle justice
The suspect being publicly shamed without a trial
The suspect being proven guilty through a fair trial in an open court of law before punishment is administered
questions.explain: The Rule of Law mandates **Due Process**. An accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a recognized court of law, ensuring punishment is fair and strictly legal.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Identify the 19th-century British constitutional scholar who fundamentally popularized the three main pillars of the **Rule of Law** (Supremacy of Law, Equality before the Law, and Fundamental Human Rights).
options: Baron de Montesquieu
Professor A.V. Dicey
Thomas Hobbes
John Locke
questions.explain: **Professor Albert Venn Dicey (A.V. Dicey)** popularized the concept of the Rule of Law in his 1885 book, *An Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution*.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following is an absolute benefit of enforcing the Rule of Law in a developing nation?
options: It strictly forbids the registration of multiple political parties
It fosters total immunity for elected Governors
It guarantees the protection of minority rights and fundamental human rights
It allows the military to interfere in daily democratic processes
questions.explain: A major **benefit of the Rule of Law** is the protection it offers. By constraining arbitrary power, it directly defends fundamental human rights and safeguards minorities from the tyranny of the majority.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: According to the democratic principle of the Rule of Law, what is the expected constitutional consequence if a highly influential billionaire breaks a criminal law?
options: They are granted total legal immunity because of their immense tax contributions
They are allowed to personally pay the police to immediately dismiss the case
They are subjected to the exact same legal processes, fair trials, and punishments as an ordinary citizen
The laws are instantly rewritten by the judge to favor the billionaire's business
questions.explain: The pillar of **Equality before the law** mandates that the law is blind to wealth or status. A billionaire who breaks the law must face the exact same judicial process and punishment as any other citizen.
